data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -N 1
#   --ntasks-per-node=4
#   --ntasks-per-socket=2
#   --cpus-per-task=7
#   -t 24:00:00
#   --gres=gpu:4
#   --mail-type=begin/end
#   --mail-user=tgartner@princeton.edu
#   (mem directive commented out)

# Map to Flux: 1 node, 4 tasks, 7 cores per task (28 cores total)
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 4
#flux: -c 7
#flux: --time-limit=24h

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:4
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without GPUs (or fewer than 4), causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: --ntasks-per-socket=2
# Flux does not have a universally portable directive for per-socket placement.
# Performance implication: rank placement/NUMA locality may differ, potentially reducing performance.

# Omitted Slurm options: --mail-type and --mail-user
# Flux does not provide a universal, built-in email notification directive in batch scripts.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but you will not receive automatic job emails.

# NOTE: Slurm dependency resubmission (sbatch --dependency=afterany:$SLURM_JOB_ID ...) has no portable Flux equivalent.
# Performance implication: the follow-on sampling job will not be scheduled automatically; you must orchestrate chaining externally.

module load cudatoolkit/10.0
module load cudnn/cuda-10.0/7.6.3
module load openmpi/gcc/3.1.3/64
source /home/tgartner/Software-deepmd-kit-1.0/tensorflow-venv/bin/activate
module load /home/tgartner/modulefiles/plumed-tg

if [ -f "Sampledone.txt" ]; then
    echo "Simulation finished"
elif ! grep -q 'ERROR' slurm* 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Continuing NPT sampling"
    # Run NPT sampling across 4 ranks.
    flux run -n 4 -c 7 /home/tgartner/Software-deepmd-kit-1.0/lammps-3Mar20/src/lmp_mpi -i in.lammps.sample -e screen
else
    echo "There is an error"
fi

reasons: The original Slurm job required 4 GPUs (`--gres=gpu:4`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH -N 1   # node count
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=4
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-socket=2
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=7
#SBATCH -t 24:00:00
# SBATCH --mem=32G
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:4
#SBATCH --mail-type=begin
#SBATCH --mail-type=end
#SBATCH --mail-user=tgartner@princeton.edu

# load environment
module load cudatoolkit/10.0
module load cudnn/cuda-10.0/7.6.3
module load openmpi/gcc/3.1.3/64
#module load fftw
source /home/tgartner/Software-deepmd-kit-1.0/tensorflow-venv/bin/activate
module load /home/tgartner/modulefiles/plumed-tg
# export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1

if [ -f "Sampledone.txt" ]; then
    echo "Simulation finished"
elif ! grep -q 'ERROR' slurm*; then
    echo "Continuing NPT sampling"
    sbatch --dependency=afterany:$SLURM_JOB_ID run.sample.qs
    # run NPT sampling
    mpirun /home/tgartner/Software-deepmd-kit-1.0/lammps-3Mar20/src/lmp_mpi -i in.lammps.sample -e screen
else
    echo "There is an error"
fi
